questions.question: Design an elevator system for a multi-storey building (LLD).
questions.title: Design an Elevator System — Low-Level Design
questions.direct_answer: Model an elevator system as an `ElevatorSystem` (controller / dispatcher) coordinating multiple `Elevator` cars in a building. **Two kinds of requests** arrive: **external hall calls** (button on a floor with direction UP/DOWN) and **internal car calls** (destination button inside the car). The dispatcher uses a **`SchedulingStrategy`** (e.g., `NearestCarStrategy`, `LookStrategy`) to assign hall calls to the best car. Each elevator runs its own state machine (`IDLE`, `MOVING_UP`, `MOVING_DOWN`, `DOOR_OPEN`) and processes its pending stops using **SCAN/LOOK** (sweep one direction, serve all stops, then reverse) — not naive FIFO. Use **interfaces** for the strategy and door behavior; use a **command queue per elevator** for thread safety. Discuss safety (overweight, door obstruction), priority (emergency, VIP) and observability (per-floor wait time).

interviewer_intent.testing: Decomposition into dispatcher + per-car state machine, the SCAN/LOOK scheduling algorithm, separation of policy via Strategy, concurrency between hall calls and car operation, and safety/edge cases.
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Naive FIFO request processing; no separation of dispatcher and elevator; ignoring direction-aware scheduling; forgetting safety (overweight, door obstruction).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: Discuss SCAN/LOOK + direction-aware merging of internal and external calls, scheduling cost function (distance + direction match), priority for emergency/maintenance, and observability.

sections.title: Problem Framing
sections.content:
An elevator system serves passengers in a multi-floor building with multiple cars:

- **Hall calls** — a passenger on floor 5 presses the UP button. The dispatcher picks one car to serve them.
- **Car calls** — inside the car, the passenger presses 9. The car adds floor 9 to its pending stops.
- The car must serve all its pending stops efficiently — not in arrival order, but by sweeping in one direction (SCAN/LOOK).
- Safety: doors don't close on people, the car doesn't overload, emergency cases preempt normal operation.

The interesting design pressure is **scheduling** (which car answers a hall call?) and **per-car movement** (in what order does this car serve its stops?), with **concurrency** between many simultaneous requests.

sections.title: Clarifying Questions
sections.content:
- **Building shape:** how many floors? How many elevator cars?
- **Direction handling:** are hall buttons direction-aware (separate UP / DOWN buttons per floor), or one button per floor?
- **Internal calls:** standard 'press destination floor' inside the car?
- **Special features:** express elevator (skips floors), service / freight elevator, VIP / emergency override?
- **Capacity / safety:** overweight detection? Door obstruction sensors?
- **Persistence:** in-memory single instance is fine for the interview?
- **Scheduling goal:** minimize average wait time, or longest wait time?

sections.title: Assumptions for This Design
sections.content:
- 20 floors, 4 elevator cars in one building.
- Direction-aware hall buttons (separate UP / DOWN).
- Internal destination buttons inside each car.
- Standard cars (no express, no freight — called out as extensions).
- Capacity limit + door-obstruction safety in scope.
- Emergency / maintenance modes called out as extensions.
- In-memory, single instance.
- Optimize average wait time.

sections.title: Core Entities and Responsibilities
sections.content:
- **`ElevatorSystem`** — receives hall calls, dispatches to an elevator using `SchedulingStrategy`. Holds the list of `Elevator`s and the strategy.
- **`Elevator`** — one car. Holds current floor, direction, state, and a `RequestQueue` of pending stops. Runs a control loop that moves between stops in SCAN/LOOK order.
- **`HallCall`** — immutable: floor, direction, timestamp.
- **`CarCall`** — immutable: floor, source elevator id.
- **`Direction`** — enum: `UP`, `DOWN`, `IDLE`.
- **`ElevatorState`** — enum: `IDLE`, `MOVING`, `DOOR_OPEN`, `OUT_OF_SERVICE`.
- **`SchedulingStrategy`** (interface) — picks the best elevator for a hall call.
  - `NearestCarStrategy` — closest by floor distance.
  - `LookStrategy` — closest car already moving in the requested direction past the requesting floor; falls back to nearest idle.
- **`DoorController`** (interface) — `open()`, `close()`, `isObstructed()`.
- **`SafetyMonitor`** — weight, door obstruction, emergency.

sections.title: Class Diagram
sections.content:
```mermaid
classDiagram
    class ElevatorSystem {
        -List~Elevator~ cars
        -SchedulingStrategy strategy
        +pressHallButton(floor, direction)
        +pressCarButton(carId, floor)
    }
    class Elevator {
        -int id
        -int currentFloor
        -Direction direction
        -ElevatorState state
        -RequestQueue requests
        -DoorController door
        -SafetyMonitor safety
        +addStop(floor)
        +step()
    }
    class RequestQueue {
        -SortedSet~Integer~ upStops
        -SortedSet~Integer~ downStops
        +add(floor, dir)
        +nextStop(currentFloor, currentDir) Optional~Integer~
    }
    class SchedulingStrategy {
        <<interface>>
        +pickCar(List~Elevator~, HallCall) Elevator
    }
    class DoorController {
        <<interface>>
        +open()
        +close()
        +isObstructed() bool
    }
    class SafetyMonitor {
        +overweight() bool
        +emergency() bool
    }

    ElevatorSystem --> Elevator
    ElevatorSystem --> SchedulingStrategy
    Elevator --> RequestQueue
    Elevator --> DoorController
    Elevator --> SafetyMonitor
    NearestCarStrategy ..|> SchedulingStrategy
    LookStrategy ..|> SchedulingStrategy
```

sections.title: Scheduling — Picking a Car for a Hall Call
Per-Car State Machine and SCAN/LOOK Movement
End-to-End Flow — Two Concurrent Hall Calls
sections.content:
```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant P1 as Passenger@F5 UP
    participant P2 as Passenger@F12 DOWN
    participant Sys as ElevatorSystem
    participant Sched as LookStrategy
    participant E1 as Elevator 1 (idle@F1)
    participant E2 as Elevator 2 (UP@F8)

    P1->>Sys: pressHallButton(5, UP)
    Sys->>Sched: pickCar(cars, call(5,UP))
    Sched-->>Sys: E1 (idle, distance 4)
    Sys->>E1: addStop(5, UP)

    P2->>Sys: pressHallButton(12, DOWN)
    Sys->>Sched: pickCar(cars, call(12,DOWN))
    Sched-->>Sys: E2 (already going UP, will reverse at top)
    Sys->>E2: addStop(12, DOWN)

    loop tick
        E1->>E1: step() — climb to F5, open door
        E2->>E2: step() — finish UP sweep, reverse to F12
    end
```

sections.title: Concurrency
Safety, Priority, and Observability
sections.content:
**Safety:**
- **Overweight:** `SafetyMonitor.overweight()` blocks door close until weight drops; refuses to start moving.
- **Door obstruction:** `DoorController.isObstructed()` re-opens the door; door close timeout retries with audible warning.
- **Emergency stop:** sets all cars to `OUT_OF_SERVICE`; opens nearest door at next floor.
- **Fire mode:** all cars go to ground floor and stop; ignore further calls.

**Priority:**
- **VIP / executive override:** marker on a hall call that boosts its scheduling priority; dispatcher picks the best car even if it must skip queued stops (advanced — mention as extension).
- **Maintenance mode:** car removed from `ElevatorSystem.cars` for the duration; calls in flight are reassigned.

**Observability:**
- Per-call wait time (button press → door open).
- Per-car utilization (% of time moving / idle).
- Number of reverses (high → scheduling is choppy).
- Histogram of stops per ride.

These metrics let you tune the cost function without guessing.

sections.title: Trade-offs and Alternatives
sections.content:
- **Scheduling: greedy (LOOK + cost function) vs full optimization** — greedy is simple and within ~10-20% of optimal; full optimization (consider all permutations of pending stops across all cars) is NP-ish and not worth it for ~4-8 cars.
- **Direction-aware vs single button per floor:** direction-aware lets the dispatcher schedule smarter; single-button is simpler but worse waiting times.
- **Tick-based vs event-driven simulation:** tick is easier to reason about and test; event-driven (next event = next floor arrival or door close) is more efficient but harder to write.
- **One worker thread per car vs central scheduler thread:** per-car gives natural isolation and parallelism; central scheduler is simpler but a single point of contention.
- **Static dispatch vs dynamic re-assignment:** a hall call assigned to car E1 is locked there. Some advanced systems re-assign mid-flight if a better car becomes free — added complexity, modest gain.
- **Express elevators / banks:** if some cars only serve odd floors / lower vs upper, partition the dispatcher; mention as extension.

sections.title: Key Points
sections.content:
- **`ElevatorSystem` (dispatcher) + `Elevator` (state machine).**
- **`SchedulingStrategy` interface** — `NearestCar`, `Look` — with a cost function (distance + direction-mismatch penalty + load).
- **SCAN/LOOK movement per car** — sweep one direction, reverse when exhausted; not FIFO.
- **`RequestQueue`** with two sorted sets (above / below current floor).
- **One worker thread per car** drives `step()`; per-car lock for queue mutation.
- **Direction-aware hall buttons** for better scheduling.
- **Safety:** overweight, door obstruction, emergency, fire mode.
- **Observability:** per-call wait time, utilization, reverses.
- **Composition + interfaces;** no `LuxuryElevator extends Elevator`.

sections.title: How to Answer This Verbally
sections.content:
**Problem framing**

Multi-floor building with multiple cars. Two kinds of requests: hall calls (passenger on floor presses UP/DOWN), car calls (passenger inside presses destination). Car must serve pending stops efficiently — not arrival order but sweeping one direction (SCAN/LOOK). Safety: doors don't close on people, no overload, emergencies preempt.

Design pressure: scheduling (which car answers a hall call?), per-car movement (in what order does this car serve its stops?), concurrency between many simultaneous requests.

**Clarifying questions**

Floors + cars count. Direction-aware hall buttons (separate UP/DOWN) or single. Internal destination buttons. Special features (express, freight, VIP). Capacity / safety. Persistence. Scheduling goal (avg wait or longest wait).

**Assumptions**

20 floors, 4 cars. Direction-aware hall buttons. Internal destination buttons inside each car. Standard cars (express/freight as extensions). Capacity + door-obstruction safety in scope. Emergency/maintenance as extensions. In-memory single instance. Optimize average wait time.

**Core entities**

ElevatorSystem: receives hall calls, dispatches via SchedulingStrategy. Holds list of Elevators + strategy.
Elevator: one car. Current floor, direction, state, RequestQueue. Worker loop moves between stops in SCAN/LOOK order.
HallCall: floor, direction, timestamp.
CarCall: floor, source elevator id.
Direction enum: UP, DOWN, IDLE.
ElevatorState enum: IDLE, MOVING, DOOR_OPEN, OUT_OF_SERVICE.
SchedulingStrategy interface: NearestCarStrategy, LookStrategy.
DoorController interface: open, close, isObstructed.
SafetyMonitor: weight, door obstruction, emergency.

**Scheduling — picking a car**

Cost function: distance(car, hall call floor) + direction-mismatch penalty (if car moving away) + load penalty (if near capacity) + idle bonus.

LookStrategy formalizes: prefer cars already moving in requested direction that haven't passed the calling floor. Fall back to idle, nearest. Last resort, cars moving opposite direction (after sweep finishes).

Well-known LOOK / SCAN-elevator approach — what real elevators use. Naive FIFO ('whichever free next') gives terrible wait times.

LookStrategy.pickCar: minBy cost. Cost = distance + (0 if moving toward in same direction; 5 if idle; 20 if moving away).

**Per-car state machine + SCAN/LOOK movement**

State machine: IDLE → MOVING (on addStop) → DOOR_OPEN (arrived) → MOVING (more stops in current direction) or IDLE (no more). Emergency → OUT_OF_SERVICE.

Movement rule: sweep current direction until no more stops in that direction, then reverse.

Elevator.addStop(floor, dir): synchronized; queue.add; if IDLE, set direction toward floor, state MOVING.

Elevator.step() called once per tick: synchronized. Get nextStop from queue; if none, IDLE. If currentFloor == target, openDoor. Else move one floor toward target.

openDoor: state DOOR_OPEN, door.open, wait for close (with obstruction check), door.close, removeStopAt currentFloor, state IDLE if queue empty else MOVING.

RequestQueue: two TreeSet<Integer> for stops above/below; nextStop returns next floor in current direction, falls back to other side when exhausted.

**End-to-end flow**

P1 at F5 presses UP → Sys calls Sched.pickCar → picks E1 (idle at F1, distance 4) → E1.addStop(5, UP).

P2 at F12 presses DOWN → Sys.pickCar picks E2 (already going UP, will reverse at top) → E2.addStop(12, DOWN).

Loop: E1 climbs to F5, opens door. E2 finishes UP sweep, reverses to F12.

**Concurrency**

Two boundaries:

1. Dispatcher receiving hall calls: many threads call pressHallButton. Mostly stateless; serialize cost computation. pickCar reads snapshots (currentFloor, direction, state) — cheap, consistent. Mark volatile or small per-car lock.

2. Per-car queue mutation: stops arrive while worker moves. addStop synchronized; step() synchronized. Lock granularity per-car; cars don't block each other.

Worker model: one dedicated thread per car (ScheduledExecutorService fixed-rate per car) drives step() loop. Each tick = one floor or one door cycle. Real systems use real time; model uses tick-based simulation.

**Safety, priority, observability**

Safety:
- Overweight: blocks door close until weight drops; refuses to start moving
- Door obstruction: re-opens door; close timeout retries with audible warning
- Emergency stop: all cars OUT_OF_SERVICE; open nearest door at next floor
- Fire mode: all cars to ground floor, stop, ignore calls

Priority:
- VIP override: marker on hall call boosts scheduling priority
- Maintenance: car removed from cars for duration; in-flight calls reassigned

Observability:
- Per-call wait time (press → door open)
- Per-car utilization (% moving / idle)
- Number of reverses (high = choppy scheduling)
- Histogram of stops per ride

Metrics let you tune the cost function without guessing.

**Trade-offs and alternatives**

- Greedy LOOK + cost function vs full optimization — greedy within 10-20% of optimal; full is NP-ish, not worth it for ~4-8 cars
- Direction-aware vs single button per floor — direction-aware schedules smarter; single simpler but worse
- Tick-based vs event-driven simulation — tick easier to test; event-driven more efficient but harder
- One worker thread per car vs central scheduler — per-car gives isolation and parallelism
- Static dispatch vs dynamic re-assignment — advanced systems re-assign mid-flight; modest gain, more complexity
- Express elevators / banks — partition dispatcher; extension

**Recommendation**

**Build an ElevatorSystem dispatcher that uses a SchedulingStrategy interface (LOOK with a cost function combining distance, direction match, load) to pick the best car for each hall call. Each Elevator runs its own state machine and serves stops in SCAN/LOOK order via a RequestQueue with two sorted sets (up/down stops). Run one worker thread per car so cars don't block each other; per-car synchronized methods protect queue mutation. Inject DoorController and SafetyMonitor as interfaces — makes overweight, obstruction, and emergency modes natural. Direction-aware hall buttons enable better scheduling. Track per-call wait time and per-car reverses to tune the cost function.**

followup_questions: Why is FIFO request processing inside a car worse than SCAN/LOOK?
How would you re-assign a hall call mid-flight if a better car becomes free?
Walk through how an emergency mode interrupts cars and clears them safely.
How do you handle a building with express elevators that only serve floors 30+?

seo.metaDescription: Low-Level Design for a multi-elevator system: dispatcher with LOOK scheduling cost function, per-car SCAN/LOOK state machine, concurrent hall + car calls, safety (overweight, door obstruction), and observability.
